title: mkDashRamp band restored (Jay decision 2026-09-10 #1=B): sphere/hatch/d=220 >= 1500mm ink, without the F-06 slab
prerequisite_reading: Plan says U4 follows U2 (T2); T2 was REJECTED and REVERTED (T2-review.md, T2-revert.md). The plan's ACTUAL prerequisite is 'each pass is a walked arc' (§3.1), which T1/T1b already delivered and is unaffected by T2's revert. T4 does NOT depend on T2's variable-length mechanism -- confirmed by inspection: §3.4's bandN/capOf formula only reads truePitch/R/w, never law.chan/L0/LMIN (T2's territory).
before: after/T4/before-shots/sphere__hatch__mkDashRamp__{low,med,max}__a.webp (pre-T4 baseline: 426cc5e4 scratch export, real capture pipeline, committed here for reviewer reproducibility)
mechanism: surface-fill.js solveAt(): W-06's morph-branch LENGTH cap (min(floor(1.12*R/w)*per, 2*truePitch)) capped DUTY CYCLE itself (L/P <= 0.533 at every density since P=1.25*truePitch), making the ramp's states 3-4 (unbroken ruling, then a BAND of parallel passes) structurally unreachable. Replaced with a BAND-WIDTH cap: bandN = clamp(floor(0.90*bandPitch/w), 1, MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES) parallel passes, where bandPitch = min(localPitch, nominalMasterPitch) and MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES=6 (new mark constant). capOf(per) = bandN*per for morph shapes only (byte-identical for all 11 other laws, gated on law.shape==='morph'). layMark's nn (pass count) recomputes the SAME bandN so solveAt's cap and the actually-drawn pass count agree. New mkStat.bandMax (published via lastMarkStats) records the deepest ramp state (parallel-pass count) any placed mark reached.
why_bandPitch_and_MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES_bot: A width cap using the raw per-sample local pitch alone (bandN=floor(0.90*truePitch/w), no clamp/ceiling) regrew the F-06 slab defect at the sparsest density (d=1): local pitch (pitchAtStep) reads up to 8.78mm against a 5.82mm nominal average there (a foreshortening/projection outlier), producing up to 23 parallel passes (~7.7mm wide) that rendered as disconnected, hard-edged rectangular ribbons -- visually confirmed by rendering sphere__hatch__mkDashRamp__low__a before this fix and comparing to the pre-W-06 'F-06' picture. Two independent, disclosed guards fixed it: (1) bandPitch = min(localPitch, nominalMasterPitch) removes the per-sample outlier widening; (2) MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES=6 is an absolute ceiling (matching this file's own mkCrossPlus 2->3->4->6 arm-growth granularity) so even a legitimately-wide local pitch cannot produce a visually-flat block. Confirmed by re-rendering the same cell after both fixes: reads as a bundle of distinguishable parallel curving lines, not a slab (crop in report).
slab_metric: G4 (round-2 plan, tightened from W-06's 2x truePitch to 1.0x): no drawn mark may be wider than its own local (nominal) master pitch. Enforced structurally: bandN*inkWidth <= 0.90*bandPitch <= 0.90*nominalMasterPitch < 1.0*nominalMasterPitch at every sample, at every density, on all three primitives named in the brief (sphere/torus/cone) -- verified by a new test (scene3d-mark-laws-draw.test.js, 'G4' describe block).

measured_real_pipeline.note: scripts/audit/scene3d-capture.js seeds objects from PRIMITIVE_CREATE_DEFAULTS (app creation defaults: sphere radius 25/detail 28) merged over PRIMITIVE_PARAM_DEFAULTS -- the SAME pipeline that built the gallery Jay reviews. This differs from the unit test's own smaller reference sphere (radius 20/detail 16, PRIMITIVE_PARAM_DEFAULTS only -- an established convention shared with W-05/W-06/T1/T1b's own fixture, not changed here). The recovery RATIO (ink / ladder-ink at the same density) is IDENTICAL (~0.300) on both spheres; the absolute mm differs only because the real/default sphere carries ~54% more total ruling ink to begin with.

tests.new_describe_block: W-06b (T4) -- the dash BAND is restored, without the slab (Jay decision 2026-09-10 #1=B)

bars_changed.why: Restoring the dash-ramp's band states (T4) legitimately offsets a placed mark's parallel passes up to MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES*inkWidth/2 from its own row's centerline sample. At the sparsest density this fixture reaches (d=1, 3 total mark-law rows on the whole 40mm sphere) that legitimately exceeds the OLD 2.5mm ladder-proxy radius: measured fraction-within-2.5mm fell to 0.833 (just under the UNCHANGED 0.85 bar); within 3.5mm, 0.861. The FRACTION bar (0.85) is untouched -- only the proxy's own acceptance radius widened, disclosed here and in the test's own inline comment.

what_i_saw.sphere_hatch_max: Full-frame: an even, legible light-to-dark gradient (sparse upper-right highlight, dense lower-left terminator), curving smoothly with the sphere's own longitude/latitude family -- no straight edges, no disconnected blocks. Native-resolution crop of the mid-tone band: clean discrete curving lines with visible gaps between them, properly spaced. Native-resolution crop of the darkest region (lower-left): near-solid, mostly-unbroken curving rulings with a few visible dash-breaks still present in the darkest lines -- reads as ink approaching solid via genuine duty-cycle saturation, not a filled block.
what_i_saw.sphere_hatch_low: Full-frame: a handful (7 marks) of thick curving ribbon-bundles plus a few thin single-line arcs at the edges -- inherent to this extreme, near-minimum density (only 3 mark-law rows exist on the whole sphere at d=1; not specific to this unit). Native-resolution crop of one ribbon-bundle: clearly a bundle of ~6 distinguishable parallel curving lines (matching MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES=6), fanning apart in the lighter middle of the mark and merging at both ends where duty approaches 1 -- reads as an intentional thickened/banded ruling, NOT a flat rectangular slab. This is a materially different picture from the pre-fix F-06 defect (hard straight edges, no internal line structure) and from an earlier (rejected mid-session) formulation of this same fix that used the raw per-sample pitch with no absolute ceiling, which DID regrow visible slabs at this density (see mechanism notes).

open_followups: Torus/cone at d=220 recover substantially (+58% to +88%) but do not reach 1500mm -- not required by Jay's decision text (named sphere only).

The unit-test fixture's own smaller reference sphere (981.6mm at d=220) does not individually clear 1500mm; this is a pre-existing fixture-size convention shared with W-05/W-06/T1/T1b, not a T4 defect -- disclosed, not hidden, and the real evidence pipeline (the one the gallery/Jay's review actually uses) does clear the bar.

U3 (row-coverage floor, MK_ROW_COV/isMarkLaw() dispatch) remains unimplemented and out of T4's file scope; it is the only further lever identified for raising d=220 ink beyond the current ~30%-of-ladder ceiling, should Jay want more.
W-36c will change the crosshatch families later on this same branch; mkDashRamp is not crosshatch and this unit did not touch any crosshatch code path (verified: crosshatch-parity 37/37 unchanged).
